_about: Occurrence-level QAC 0.4 corrections and selected contextual analyses, adjudicated from the vocalised Uthmani word, governing particles, primary verse i'rab, the reference fork and reviewed lexemes. Raw metadata and source tags stay unchanged. Applied consistently to packets, validation, assembly and audit counts; every change is documented.

18:1:11.noteEnglish: QAC tags عِوَجَا nominative, but it ends in fatha + alif (tanwin al-fath, read ʿiwajā at Hafs' saktah) and is the object of jussive يَجْعَل: accusative.

18:13:10.noteEnglish: QAC tags وَزِدْنَـٰهُمْ PERF PASS with نَا as na'ib al-fa'il. It is active: نَا is the subject (We increased them), هُمْ the first object and هُدًى the second object (QAC's own 18:13 note: «هدى» مفعول ثانٍ; all translations active). The 1P perfect زِدْنَا is spelled the same in both voices.

18:20:3.noteEnglish: QAC tags يَظْهَرُوا۟ subjunctive; it is the jussive verb of the conditional إِنْ (its nun dropped for jazm), answered by jussive يَرْجُمُوكُمْ.

18:20:5.noteEnglish: QAC tags يَرْجُمُوكُمْ subjunctive, but no particle of nasb precedes it; it is the jussive answer (jawab al-shart) of the conditional إِن يَظْهَرُوا۟, and the dropped nun is the sign of jazm.

18:20:7.noteEnglish: QAC tags يُعِيدُوكُمْ subjunctive; it is joined by أَوْ to the jussive answer يَرْجُمُوكُمْ of the conditional إِن يَظْهَرُوا۟, so it is jussive too (the dropped nun is the sign of jazm).

18:29:19.noteEnglish: QAC tags يَسْتَغِيثُوا۟ subjunctive; it is the jussive verb of the conditional وَإِن (nun dropped for jazm).

18:29:20.noteEnglish: QAC omits PASS and tags subjunctive. يُغَاثُوا۟ is the Form IV passive (active would be يُغِيثُوا) and the jussive answer of the conditional; its waw is na'ib al-fa'il.

18:82:33.noteEnglish: QAC gives تَسْطِع no mood; after لَمْ it is jussive (the sukun/absent final vowel is the sign of jazm).

18:110:6.noteEnglish: QAC tags يُوحَىٰٓ subjunctive, but no particle of nasb precedes it; it is indicative with an implied damma (للتعذر) and passive Form IV.

23:27:27.noteEnglish: QAC tags تُخَاطِبْنِى 3rd person feminine singular; it follows prohibitive لَا and addresses Nuh: 2nd person masculine singular jussive.

23:35:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags مِتُّمْ passive. Hafs' kasra form is the active dialectal perfect of مَاتَ (as in خِفْتُ from خَافَ), intransitive with no personal passive; translations render it active ('you die').

23:37:7.noteEnglish: QAC tags نَحْيَا subjunctive, but no particle of nasb precedes it (نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا); it is indicative with an implied damma.

23:62:12.noteEnglish: QAC tags يُظْلَمُونَ jussive; the retained nun after negative لا shows it is indicative (passive).

23:82:3.noteEnglish: QAC tags مِتْنَا passive; as in 23:35, Hafs' kasra form is the active dialectal perfect of مَاتَ.

23:91:17.noteEnglish: QAC's lemma taEa`laY` merges two verbs. وَلَعَلَا here is Form I عَلَا يَعْلُو (would have overpowered), not Form VI تَعَالَى; it gets its own paradigm card.

23:92:4.noteEnglish: QAC gives فَتَعَـٰلَىٰ no form tag (Form I); it is Form VI تَعَالَى (tafāʿala, defective), as the mustafa0x fork tags it.

23:116:1.noteEnglish: QAC gives فَتَعَـٰلَى no form tag (Form I); it is Form VI تَعَالَى (tafāʿala, defective), as the mustafa0x fork tags it.

32:11:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags يَتَوَفَّىٰكُم subjunctive, but nothing governs nasb after قُلْ; it is indicative with an implied damma.

36:10:6.noteEnglish: QAC tags تُنذِرْهُمْ 3rd person feminine singular; in ءَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنذِرْهُمْ it is 2nd person masculine singular, jussive after لَمْ, parallel to أَنذَرْتَ.

36:20:6.noteEnglish: QAC tags يَسْعَىٰ subjunctive; it is an indicative verbal sentence describing رَجُلٌ (QAC's own ayah note makes it a نعت), with an implied damma.

36:54:3.noteEnglish: QAC tags تُظْلَمُ active and jussive. The prefix vowel u with fatha on the lam makes it passive (no soul will be wronged), نَفْسٌ is its na'ib al-fa'il, and after negative لَا it is indicative (final damma).

36:78:8.noteEnglish: QAC tags يُحْىِ jussive, but مَن here is interrogative and nothing governs jazm; it is indicative. Its second ya is not written before the hamzat al-wasl of ٱلْعِظَـٰمَ.

55:27:1.noteEnglish: QAC tags وَيَبْقَىٰ subjunctive, but no particle governs it; it is indicative with an implied damma, coordinated with the nominal sentence of 55:26.

18:18:6.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ذَاتَ ٱلْيَمِينِ is an adverb of place (ظرفِ مکان) of نُقَلِّبُهُمْ, accusative with fatha.

18:18:8.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. وَذَاتَ ٱلشِّمَالِ is coordinated with the adverb ذَاتَ ٱلْيَمِينِ: accusative with fatha.

18:18:12.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ذِرَاعَيْهِ is the object of the active participle بَـٰسِطٌ; the dual ya ending marks the accusative.

18:32:7.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. جَنَّتَيْنِ is the object of جَعَلْنَا; the dual ya ending marks the accusative.

18:33:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ٱلْجَنَّتَيْنِ is the muḍāf ilayh of كِلْتَا; the dual ya ending marks the genitive.

18:46:6.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word GEN, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. وَٱلْبَـٰقِيَـٰتُ is the subject (مبتدا) of the new sentence, with خَيْرٌ as predicate: nominative with damma.

18:46:7.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word GEN, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتُ is the adjective of nominative ٱلْبَـٰقِيَـٰتُ: nominative with damma.

18:49:9.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. يَـٰوَيْلَتَنَا: an annexed vocative (منادیٰ مضاف) is accusative, here with visible fatha.

18:52:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. شُرَكَآءِىَ is the object of نَادُوا۟; accusative with an implied fatha (the kasra precedes the first-person ya).

18:56:15.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ءَايَـٰتِى is the first object of ٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ (هُزُوًا the second); accusative, the sign implied before the first-person ya.

18:82:5.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. يَتِيمَيْنِ is the adjective of genitive لِغُلَـٰمَيْنِ; the dual ya ending marks the genitive.

18:93:5.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ٱلسَّدَّيْنِ is the muḍāf ilayh of the adverb بَيْنَ; the dual ya ending marks the genitive.

18:96:8.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ٱلصَّدَفَيْنِ is the muḍāf ilayh of بَيْنَ; the dual ya ending marks the genitive.

18:98:9.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. رَبِّى in وَعْدُ رَبِّى is muḍāf ilayh: genitive (sign implied before the first-person ya).

18:98:14.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. رَبِّى in وَعْدُ رَبِّى is muḍāf ilayh: genitive (sign implied before the first-person ya).

18:102:6.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. عِبَادِى is the first object of يَتَّخِذُوا۟: accusative (sign implied before the first-person ya).

18:106:7.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ءَايَـٰتِى is the first object of ٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟: accusative (sign implied before the first-person ya).

18:106:8.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. وَرُسُلِى is coordinated with the object ءَايَـٰتِى: accusative (sign implied before the first-person ya).

18:109:7.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. رَبِّى in لِّكَلِمَـٰتِ رَبِّى is muḍāf ilayh: genitive.

18:109:14.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. رَبِّى in كَلِمَـٰتُ رَبِّى is muḍāf ilayh: genitive.

23:23:7.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. يَـٰقَوْمِ: an annexed vocative (منادیٰ مضاف) is accusative; the visible kasra signals the first-person ya, so the nasb is implied.

23:26:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. رَبِّ (يا محذوفة): an annexed vocative (منادیٰ مضاف) is accusative; the visible kasra signals the first-person ya, so the nasb is implied.

23:39:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. رَبِّ (يا محذوفة): an annexed vocative (منادیٰ مضاف) is accusative; the visible kasra signals the first-person ya, so the nasb is implied.

23:93:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. رَّبِّ (يا محذوفة): an annexed vocative (منادیٰ مضاف) is accusative; the visible kasra signals the first-person ya, so the nasb is implied.

23:94:1.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. رَبِّ (يا محذوفة): an annexed vocative (منادیٰ مضاف) is accusative; the visible kasra signals the first-person ya, so the nasb is implied.

23:97:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. رَّبِّ (يا محذوفة): an annexed vocative (منادیٰ مضاف) is accusative; the visible kasra signals the first-person ya, so the nasb is implied.

23:118:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. رَّبِّ (يا محذوفة): an annexed vocative (منادیٰ مضاف) is accusative; the visible kasra signals the first-person ya, so the nasb is implied.

23:27:17.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. زَوْجَيْنِ is the object of فَٱسْلُكْ (مِن كُلٍّ with tanwin in Hafs); the dual ya ending marks the accusative.

23:27:18.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ٱثْنَيْنِ is the adjective of accusative زَوْجَيْنِ; accusative with the dual ya ending.

23:50:9.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ذَاتِ is the adjective of genitive رَبْوَةٍ: genitive with kasra.

23:110:5.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ذِكْرِى is the second object of أَنسَوْكُمْ: accusative (sign implied before the first-person ya).

36:14:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ٱثْنَيْنِ is the object of أَرْسَلْنَآ; the dual ya ending marks the accusative.

36:26:6.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. قَوْمِى is the noun (اسم) of لَيْتَ: accusative (sign implied before the first-person ya).

36:52:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. يَـٰوَيْلَنَا: an annexed vocative (منادیٰ مضاف) is accusative, here with visible fatha.

55:12:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word GEN, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. In the Hafs reading وَٱلرَّيْحَانُ is nominative, coordinated with ٱلْحَبُّ (damma visible); the genitive tag reflects another reading.

55:17:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ is the muḍāf ilayh of رَبُّ; the dual ya ending marks the genitive.

55:17:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. ٱلْمَغْرِبَيْنِ is the muḍāf ilayh of رَبُّ; the dual ya ending marks the genitive.

55:33:1.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. يَـٰمَعْشَرَ: an annexed vocative (منادیٰ مضاف) is accusative with fatha.

23:45:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. وَأَخَاهُ is coordinated with the object مُوسَىٰ of أَرْسَلْنَا: accusative, marked by alif as one of the five nouns.

23:64:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags this word NOM, contradicting the vocalised form and its role. مُتْرَفِيهِم is the object of أَخَذْنَا: accusative, marked by the sound-plural ya (nun dropped before the pronoun).

18:12:7.noteEnglish: QAC tags the stem of لِمَا REL, deriving pronoun, but the primary 18:12 verse i‘rab explicitly calls ما مصدرية. Follow the selected masdar-particle analysis: lam governs the interpreted masdar, attached to an implied hal of amadan. The effective app word type is particle; preserve raw QAC tags and exact Arabic.

18:22:19.noteEnglish: QAC tags مَّا REL, deriving pronoun, but the primary 18:22 verse analysis makes قليل the subject of ما يعلمهم إلا قليل and إلا restrictive. Ma is the non-governing negative particle here, not a relative noun. The effective app word type is particle; preserve raw QAC tags and exact Arabic.

18:26:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags the stem of بِمَا REL, deriving pronoun, but the primary 18:26 verse i‘rab explicitly calls ما مصدرية and لبثوا the clause of the حرفي موصول. Follow the selected masdar-particle analysis, with the interpreted masdar governed by bi and attached to أعلم. The effective app word type is particle; preserve raw QAC tags and exact Arabic.

23:26:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags the stem of بِمَا REL, deriving pronoun, but the primary 23:26 verse i‘rab explicitly calls ما مصدرية and bi causal, with the interpreted masdar attached to انصرني. Follow that selected contextual analysis. The effective app word type is particle; preserve raw QAC tags and exact Arabic.

23:39:4.noteEnglish: QAC tags the stem of بِمَا REL, deriving pronoun, but the primary 23:39 verse i‘rab explicitly calls ما مصدرية, with كذبون its clause and the interpreted masdar attached to انصرني. Follow that selected contextual analysis. The effective app word type is particle; preserve raw QAC tags and exact Arabic.

32:9:13.noteEnglish: QAC tags مَّا REL, deriving pronoun, but the primary 32:9 verse i‘rab explicitly calls ما زائدة, after قليلا functioning as نائب مفعول مطلق. Follow the extra-particle analysis, with no case position or relative clause. The effective app word type is particle; preserve raw QAC tags and exact Arabic.

32:14:2.noteEnglish: QAC tags the first بِمَا of 32:14 REL, deriving pronoun, but the primary verse i‘rab explicitly calls this ما مصدرية, with the interpreted masdar attached to فذوقوا. Follow that selected causal masdar-particle analysis. The effective app word type is particle; preserve raw QAC tags and exact Arabic.

36:32:3.noteEnglish: QAC tags لَّمَّا T, deriving noun, but the primary 36:32 verse i‘rab explicitly calls لما أداة حصر بمعنى إلا, paired with negative إن. Follow the restrictive-particle analysis, not temporal or jussive lamma. The effective app word type is particle; preserve raw QAC tags and exact Arabic.
